Photograph: Santiago Mazzarovich/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Rebeca Grynspan’s parents were refugees from the Holocaust. If elected she would be the UN’s first Jewish secretary general. Photograph: Santiago Mazzarovich/AFP/Getty Images United Nations Costa Rican diplomat emerges as strong contender to be first female head of UN Rebeca Grynspan seen as continuity candidate with tacit support from current secretary general, António Guterres Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor Sun 9 Aug 2026 03.00 EDT Last modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 03.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Costa Rican diplomat and former vice-president whose parents were refugees from the Holocaust has become the surprise frontrunner to lead the United Nations as its first female secretary general. Rebeca Grynspan, whose parents emigrated to Central America from Poland – and whose maternal grandparents were killed by the Nazis – is the current head of the UN conference on trade and development (UNCTAD), a body that has exhaustively tallied the economic damage inflicted by Israel’s occupation of the Palestinian territories. The current secretary general, António Guterres, will complete his second term on 31 December 2026 and under an informal system of regional rotation his successor is expected to come from Latin America. In a secret first straw poll of the UN security council, the five permanent and 10 temporary members were asked to say whether they supported, objected to or were neutral about each of seven candidates. Grynspan secured 10 “encourage” votes, four “no opinion” votes and one “discourage” vote. The identity of the discourage vote is not known, but the fact that she had only one objection places her in a strong opening position. The process is likely to conclude in October. Grynspan’s closest rival is Carolyn Rodrigues-Burkett, Guyana’s former UN envoy, with nine encourages, two discourages and four no opinions. At the close of a Bloomberg-sponsored debate at the general assembly last month she secured 49% of the vote among those attending, with Grynspan second on 14%. “Grynspan is seen by some as the continuity candidate, having the tacit support from Guterres,” said one western diplomat. “But the key is the source of the candidate’s discouragement votes: if [the votes] are coming from Russia, China or the US, there is a risk of deadlock.” The election comes at a critical moment for the legitimacy of multilateralism, as the UN suffers 20% job cuts and the secretary general’s role as mediator is supplanted by other actors, leaving the world body as a largely ignored moral conscience, or as a venue in which all sides vent their well-rehearsed differences. If elected, Grynspan would be the UN’s first Jewish secretary general. The UN has been criticised for overly focusing on Israel in its debates, but Grynspan has invoked her Jewish heritage to argue for the importance of ending conflict. She told the UN general assembly: “Peace is what made it possible for my parents, two refugees from the second world war, to find respect and dignity in a small country, Costa Rica . I am the daughter of this peace, a demonstration of what peace makes possible.” Her sister moved to Israel as a 17-year-old to study chemistry at the Hebrew University. As a result, her niece and nephew have completed compulsory service in the Israel Defense Forces. Under her leadership, however, UNCTAD has factually and starkly documented the economic damage wrought by Israel’s long-term occupation of the Palestinian territories. Its landmark February 2026 report found that “cumulatively, the Palestinian economy lost an estimated $212.2bn (in constant 2015 dollars) from 2000 to 2024. This partial, estimated lost potential, equivalent to nearly 20 times the entire Palestinian GDP of 2024, stems directly from Israeli occupation policies, restrictions, closures, and recurrent military operations.” In November 2025 Grynspan pointed out that Gaza’s GDP per capita had plummeted to $161 per person per year, one of the most severe economic contractions in modern history. Three other candidates, including Michelle Bachelet, have probably met with too much influential opposition to secure the job. Bachelet, the former president of Chile and a former UN human rights commissioner, faces opposition from the US government, which claims she was soft on China’s human rights record. But the Trump administration’s recent suggestion that the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, should get the job symbolises America’s drift away from the UN mainstream. The secretary general is elected to serve an initial four-year term after the 193-strong general assembly is requested to endorse a single recommendation by the security council. A candidate needs nine positive votes and no veto by a security council member. The new candidate must be elected by the end of the year, and there will be further meetings of the security council to test opinion. https://www.hospitalityireland.com/gener.text: With the summer holidays entering their final stretch, thousands of families are expected to snap up late deals and jet off for one final week of sunshine before children return to the classroom. New figures from package holiday specialists On the Beach, reveal that 11.9% of Irish summer bookings are now made at the last minute, with holidaymakers securing trips departing within just 14 days. With only two weeks of the school holidays remaining, searches for holidays departing during the final week have jumped by 22% in the past 48 hours alone. 'Historic Summer' "After a historic summer of sport and plenty of All-Ireland excitement, thousands of families are realising there’s still time to squeeze in one last escape before the uniforms come out and the alarm clocks go back on," said Caspar Nelson, holiday expert at On the Beach. “We’re seeing a huge surge in searches for holidays departing during the final week, pointing to a major last-minute booking rush." ADVERTISEMENT According to On the Beach, Spain is leading the last-minute getaway rush, with the Canary Islands and Greece also among the most searched-for destinations for the final week of the school holidays. The top ten most searched for destinations include: 1. Spain 2. Canary Islands 3. Greece 4. Turkey 5. Portugal 6. Balearic Islands 7. Czech Republic 8. Netherlands 9. Belgium 10. Germany "Irish holidaymakers are clearly comfortable waiting until the eleventh hour, with many booking, packing and flying within a matter of days,” said Caspar Nelson.

https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/.text: Front Page Taiwan News Business Editorial & Opinion Sports World News Features Bilingual Pages Search Search All Front Page Taiwan News Business Editorial & Opinion Sports World News Features Bilingual Pages GO Home Taiwan News Six lawmakers face corruption charges this term By Lin Che-yuan and Sam Garcia / Staff reporter, with staff writer Add TT as Preferred Source Six legislators from across party lines have been indicted for corruption during the current legislative term, highlighting a broader pattern of legal controversies in the legislature. This morning, the Taipei and Lienchiang County offices of Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) Legislator Chen Hsueh-sheng (陳雪生) were searched over allegations that he lobbied on behalf of a company that funded one of his assistants, becoming the latest in a series of judicial investigations into lawmakers this term. He has not been charged. Prosecutors carry boxes of evidence from the Taipei offices of Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) Legislator Chen Hsueh-sheng this morning. Photo: Wang Yi-sung, Taipei Times In addition to the six lawmakers indicted for corruption, six KMT legislators have been reported or named as defendants over alleged contraventions of the Anti-Infiltration Act (反滲透法), document forgery and leaking secrets. Seven KMT and three Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) legislators have been indicted on assault charges stemming from physical altercations in the legislature. FRAUD CASES Independent Legislator May Chin (高金素梅) was indicted on charges of corruption and fraud over allegations that she used friends and relatives as nominal assistants to fraudulently claim more than NT$7.87 million (US$247,010) in expenses and illegally imported COVID-19 rapid test kits from China. The Taipei District Prosecutors’ Office is seeking a 12-year and six-month sentence. DPP Legislator Lin Dai-hua (林岱樺) was indicted over allegations that she used nominal aides and inflated overtime claims to fraudulently obtain nearly NT$15 million, as well as misappropriating benefits through a foundation and temple. The case is currently under trial. KMT Legislator Yen Kuan-heng (顏寬恒) was accused of falsely claiming to have purchased and sold state-owned land, as well as forging documents and fraudulently claiming aide expenses. He was convicted in both the first and second trials and handed a prison sentence of eight years and four months, but the Supreme Court later overturned the corruption conviction and sent the case back for a retrial. DPP Legislator Lin I-chin (林宜瑾) was indicted over allegations that she fraudulently claimed more than NT$14.12 million in aide expenses, with the Tainan District Court sentencing her to seven years in prison in the first trial. The ruling is subject to appeal. KMT Legislator Sra Kacaw (鄭天財) was accused of accepting NT$7.11 million in bribes and receiving financial support from nine business owners. Taipei prosecutors indicted him on corruption and other charges and are seeking a sentence of more than 10 years. KMT Legislator Chen Chao-ming (陳超明) was implicated in a corruption case involving SOGO and accused of accepting NT$1 million in political donations. He was sentenced to seven years and eight months in prison in the first trial, but acquitted on appeal. INFILTRATION, FORGERY CASES KMT caucus whip Fu Kun-chi (傅崐萁) was accused of using the company Zhan Tian Xia (戰天下) to provide legislators with discounted campaign merchandise, potentially contravening the Business Entity Accounting Act (商業會計法), Anti-Infiltration Act (反滲透法) and forging documents KMT legislators Hsu Yu-chen (許宇甄) and Sasuyu Ruljuwan (盧縣一) were indicted over allegedly fraudulent signatures in a recall petition targeting DPP Legislator Wu Li-hua (伍麗華). KMT Legislator Ma Wen-chun (馬文君) was named a defendant in an investigation into alleged leaks of classified information related to Taiwan’s indigenous defense submarine program. KMT Legislator Hsu Chiao-hsin (徐巧芯) was named a defendant in an investigation into alleged leaks of documents related to Ukraine aid via the Czech Republic. KMT Legislator Cheng Cheng-chien (鄭正鈐) was named a defendant in an investigation into allegations that he accepted Chinese Communist Party funding and leaked information to China’s Taiwan Affairs Office. LEGISLATURE FIGHTS Several physical altercations broke out in the Legislative Yuan during plenary sessions in 2024 and last year, leading Taipei prosecutors this year to indict KMT legislators Hsieh Lung-chieh (謝龍介), Liao Wei-hsiang (廖偉翔), Chiu Cheng-chun (邱鎮軍), Huang Chien-hao (黃健豪), Huang Jen (黃仁), Wang Hung-wei (王鴻薇) and Chen Yu-jen (陳玉珍). Also indicted were DPP legislators Lin Shu-fen (林淑芬), Michelle Lin (林楚茵) and Ker Chien-ming (柯建銘) on assault and other charges. Photograph: Ibraheem Abu Mustafa/Reuters View image in fullscreen Saudi Arabia says it shot down a Houthi drone close to the holy city of Mecca. Photograph: Ibraheem Abu Mustafa/Reuters Saudi Arabia Saudi Arabia warns of ‘red line’ after Houthi drone intercepted close to holy city of Mecca The Iran-aligned militant group rejected the suggestion it had targeted Mecca, while the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation condemned the attack Agencies Tue 15 Sep 2026 21.56 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Saudi Arabia’s air defences intercepted and destroyed a ⁠Houthi drone south of Mecca on Tuesday before it entered prohibited airspace over the holy city, according to a ⁠spokesperson for the ⁠Saudi-led ​military coalition which is fighting the Iran-aligned group in Yemen . The security of Islam’s two holiest sites and of pilgrims was a “red line”, ⁠coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said early on Wednesday, adding that the coalition would take necessary deterrent measures against the ⁠Houthis. Mecca, home to shrines sacred to Muslims worldwide, is Islam’s holiest ​city and the focal point ‌of the annual ‌hajj pilgrimage, one of the five pillars of Islam, which millions of Muslims ‌undertake each year. The rapid Houthi advance in Yemen: why it matters and what’s at stake Read more Malki described the incident as the second Houthi attempt to target Mecca, after what the coalition said was a ballistic missile launch in July 2017. A Houthi official rejected the claim on Wednesday, with spokesperson Hazem al-Assad writing on X: “The claims about targeting Mecca are a worn-out lie that has been used before and no longer fools anyone.” The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation condemned what they called a “heinous” attack on Islam’s holy city, blaming the Houthis. The group – which is made up of 57 Muslim-majority countries decried the “ongoing aggression against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia .” Saudi Arabia issued security alerts across parts of the country on Tuesday, including in Mecca and other ‌cities, following a week of attacks by Iran-aligned fighters that have drawn the kingdom deeper into the Middle East ​war. The Houthis have seized control of parts of ⁠Yemen’s Red Sea coast overlooking the Bab al-Mandab, one of the ​world’s most important ​shipping straits, threatening Saudi oil ​exports rerouted from the strait of Hormuz. The group has ​announced several major ‌attacks on ​Saudi Arabia over ​the past week, including strikes on an airbase on Monday that it said were retaliation for airstrikes on Yemen . INTERNATIONAL Romanian authorities launch rescue as 8 people go missing in Black Sea ship fire By: Agencies Date: October 16, 2026 Share post: WhatsApp Facebook X ReddIt Telegram Linkedin Bucharest, Oct 15: Romanian authorities launched search and rescue operations off the Black Sea coast Thursday after a fire broke out on board a ship, leaving eight people missing. Four were rescued. The cause of the fire aboard the San Marino-flagged Wine Trader, a chemical tanker travelling from Tunisia to Romania, was not immediately clear, but a recent spate of drone strikes on ships in the Black Sea has raised fears of Russia’s war in Ukraine spreading. A “group of air targets” was monitored overnight near Ukraine’s Snake Island, and a drone briefly entered Romania’s airspace at 1:34 am southeast of Sulina, before disappearing from radar, according to Romania’s Ministry of National Defence. There were 12 people aboard the ship when the fire broke out 13 nautical miles southeast of the port town of Sulina, according to the Romanian Naval Authority. Similar drone incursions have occurred this month in the exclusive economic zones of Romania and Bulgaria, both NATO and European Union members. A fire was reported on the Comoros-flagged Yara J, a chemical and oil tanker travelling from Turkey to Sulina, Romania, on Wednesday evening in Romanian territorial waters. The crew was safe. Romania’s acting Defense Minister Radu Miruta said an investigation was underway but that no drone was seen on military radars heading toward that tanker. On Tuesday, drone strikes on two ships off Bulgaria prompted emergency rescue operations for 11 crew members from the HS Dignity, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship, who remain missing. The other ship, a Ukrainian-operated coastal freighter named Chelsea 3, was sailing under a Maltese flag. Rescuers evacuated all 15 crew members, with five receiving treatment for minor injuries. The crew reported the ship’s deck and hull were hit by three aerial drones. The Tuesday incidents, for which Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said Russia was likely responsible for, came a week after sea and aerial drones struck two other vessels.
